reason: Both are polished native sign-in screens with strong dark modes, but B keeps both social buttons usable at AX-XL, uses explicit field labels, and shows realistic filled content. A’s largest text size blows up the headline and clips everything below the Apple button.

A has a clearer form hierarchy, specific copy, tighter label alignment, and a more carefully stepped dark mode. B’s centered logo stack is prettier but generic, and AX-XL pushes the sign-in controls off-screen much sooner.

B’s hero, type ramp, and buy bar stay aligned and readable at AX-XL. A hides Color under the sticky bar and truncates the title, price, and CTA at large text, while repeating the discount as a badge, strikethrough, and pill.

A has a clearer hero-to-price path, tighter accent use, and type that still fits at AX-XL. B duplicates the discount, lets the sticky bar cover color, and truncates the title, price, and CTA at large text.

B has a clearer type ramp and a single dominant amount, with fewer competing controls. Large text wraps the greeting instead of truncating it. A’s chip row and overlapping Add expense weaken hierarchy, and AX-XL clips the header and covers summary data.
B’s hero amount dominates and dark mode uses a deliberate light surface on dark chrome. A’s AX-XL layout overflows and clips; B’s primary card reflows, though both still overlap the add button.

B keeps the balance intact at AX-XL and uses cleaner native toolbar chrome. A’s green card is stronger in light and dark, but the hero amount splits to “$12,847.” / “33”, search truncates, and chips clip.

A’s balance card, green/red money semantics, and aligned type feel tighter and more native. B has richer transactions and a stronger dark theme, but the mint wash and the AX balance splitting after the decimal look unfinished.

B wins on execution: no clipped label at default size, and large text wraps instead of truncating while the terms footer stays readable. A clips 'Talk, don't type' in light and dark and overlaps the sign-in row at AX-XL. Shared strengths are the headline, realistic memo preview, and designed dark surfaces.

A is the more finished screen: even spacing, a high-contrast CTA, and a designed dark mode. B has a stronger headline and more specific copy, but a chip is clipped at default size and the pale button loses the focal action. Both collapse at AX-XL.

A reads as a finished paywall: clearer path to the trial CTA, correct Close/Restore placement, tuned dark accent, and specific pricing copy. B’s monthly/yearly cards are illegible in both modes, nav actions are swapped, and AX text truncates. Both break at AX-XL.

B has clearer hierarchy, a real price disclosure, legal links, and text that still wraps at AX-XL. A’s plan control collides with the CTA, and large text truncates copy and drops the offer. Neither shows readable monthly and yearly plans.

A is more visually resolved: accent selection, member metadata, tracked headers, and ellipsis truncation. B has truer product copy, but splits the email mid-word at AX-XL. Both omit subscription and collapse under large text.

A’s fieldnote.app copy is specific and the screen stays quieter. B’s example.com address and five accent swatches feel more template-like. Both omit subscription and account depth and both break at AX-XL.

A has a clearer hero number, tighter restraint, and de-emphasized units, and it reflows cleanly at AX-XL. B’s donut competes with the distance, extra chrome and track bars add noise, and the goal line breaks mid-phrase at large text.

A is the more designed screen: one accent, a purposeful goal ring, exact internal stats, and a dark mode with real surface steps. B is clearer at a glance and reflows better at AX-XL, but the icon-card grid, extra green accent, and tiny unscaled chevrons feel templated.
